transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's curriculum-approval meeting. As you know, the partner high school has proposed a dual-credit environmental science course for the spring term, and I have the authority to approve it and its operating details once we've reviewed everything. The draft proposal lists a maximum enrollment of 28 students, three credits, and Ms. Patel as the instructor, with the course counting toward both the high-school science program and students' community-college transcripts. Before I sign off on this, I'd like to hear from each of you — the proposed teacher, the registrar, and the dual-credit liaison — regarding any information that needs to be reflected in the proposal before approval. Please go ahead.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a concern before we proceed. I inspected the planned laboratory room and found that the room's fixed workstations and required aisle clearance allow no more than 20 students for this course. I recorded the measurement in my classroom notes but haven't yet attached it to the curriculum proposal. The draft proposal's maximum enrollment of 28 students would exceed the room's safe capacity, so I believe the enrollment cap needs to be revised down to 20 before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a discrepancy regarding the course code and credit value. My transcript crosswalk, which I confirmed with the community-college records office, requires this dual-credit course to use the exact course code ENV-115 and carry exactly 4 college credits. The draft proposal currently lists three credits, and neither the correct course code nor the correct credit value has been entered in the high-school scheduling system yet. These details need to be corrected before approval is signed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to disclose an important requirement from the signed articulation memorandum on file in my partnership records. That memorandum was not included with the draft proposal, but it specifies that I, Dr. Lewis, must teach the first six weeks of the inaugural offering of this course. This is because Ms. Patel does not yet have the graduate-level coursework required for dual-credit instruction. The proposal currently lists Ms. Patel as the instructor with no mention of this co-teaching arrangement, so this needs to be reflected before approval is signed.
